title: Impersonation provenance is stamped synchronously on every audit entry
decision:
- Synchronous `QueuedAuditLogger::record()` is the universal stamp seam. When an
  impersonation state exists it overwrites actor to support/staff and merges an
  immutable context containing grant, target effective user and reason.
- `ImpersonationState` gains an additive optional reason carrier for constructor
  compatibility; the real tenancy service always supplies a non-empty reason.
- Starting while a state is active fails before another grant is consumed. Initiator
  and target cannot change inside a session.
- Expiry or revocation closes the session before the next protected request proceeds.
  P12 does not claim interruption of an already-running request.
- Failed target login clears session/auth state and records a failed start while the
  one-time grant remains consumed. Existing three write guards and their allow
  semantics are not loosened.
rationale:
Enriching only the model observer leaves explicit audit callers as a compliance hole.
The enqueue seam still has request/session context and already owns event-time and
workspace snapshots, so it is the one complete location.

sections.title: D64 — Impersonation provenance is stamped synchronously on every audit entry
sections.text:
**Actor:** plan-designer/codex-gpt-5.6-sol/high
**Evidence:** RAG:— `AuditObserver` uses `CurrentActor`, but direct
`AuditLogger::record()` callers can omit impersonation context; active state does not
carry grant reason and `start()` does not explicitly reject nesting. RAG:✅ GCP audit
logs preserve caller and impersonated identity; AWS source identity persists through
assumed sessions and temporary credentials require expiry/revocation controls.

sections.title: Решение
sections.text:
- Synchronous `QueuedAuditLogger::record()` is the universal stamp seam. When an
  impersonation state exists it overwrites actor to support/staff and merges an
  immutable context containing grant, target effective user and reason.
- `ImpersonationState` gains an additive optional reason carrier for constructor
  compatibility; the real tenancy service always supplies a non-empty reason.
- Starting while a state is active fails before another grant is consumed. Initiator
  and target cannot change inside a session.
- Expiry or revocation closes the session before the next protected request proceeds.
  P12 does not claim interruption of an already-running request.
- Failed target login clears session/auth state and records a failed start while the
  one-time grant remains consumed. Existing three write guards and their allow
  semantics are not loosened.

sections.title: Почему
sections.text:
Enriching only the model observer leaves explicit audit callers as a compliance hole.
The enqueue seam still has request/session context and already owns event-time and
workspace snapshots, so it is the one complete location.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.text:
P12.6 changes only core audit/state. P12.7 changes tenancy lifecycle/session behavior
and proves nested, failed-login, expiry, revocation and write-policy negative cases.
